title: Bring your Designs to Life in Unreal Engine with LiveSync 2
content:
## _Hey creators,_

We are excited to announce that **CLO LiveSync 2.0.0 has just been released** for CLO 2025.0! MD LiveSync 2.0.0 will be available when MD 2025.0 is released. 

What's new in LiveSync 2.0.0? The UI and workflow have been reworked to shorten the process of bringing Marvelous CLOthes to Unreal Engine, and support for macOS has been finally added! 

![d94dc12fab5e440d8ec345b468d113bd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/ab037770b24049bd9426486574a4e1fc/images/d94dc12fab5e440d8ec345b468d113bdlivesync2-promo-image.png)

You can access the macOS version when CLO/MD LiveSync becomes on [Fab.com](http://Fab.com) in the coming days.For more information about improvements and bug fixes, please take a look at [the release note](https://support-connect.clo-set.com/hc/en-us/articles/8924444885775-CLO-LiveSync).

title: Super Heros
content:
## _Explore the imaginative realm of Lucas Camargo, also known as UntitledArmy, who uses Marvelous Designer to create stop-motion look animations featuring unique character designs._

* * *

# **Interview with**[**Lucas Camargo**](https://www.behance.net/untitledarmy)**| Creative Director**

* * *

# **Please introduce yourself to the Marvelous Designer community.**

Hi, I am the artist Lucas Camargo, a.k.a. UntitledArmy. I am a Creative Director, Freelance Illustrator, Artist, and Director. I create unique and thoughtful characters, designs, and ideas. I have worked in the creative industry for the last 20+ years, starting in advertising and then switching to 3D animation, and now I am a full-time artist.

# **Let’s talk about your recent project, “Super Heros”. Can you tell us where you got the inspiration for the concept or what was the visual style you were aiming for?**

I love designing characters, thinking of different and unique approaches, and unexpected ways in a certain idea or universe. I often play around with some well-known characters to exercise what would be my approach, taking something that has been done to exhaustion is a good exercise to do, so I started with SpiderMan, and played with different silhouettes, thinking what if he had more a spider proportion, and from that I made some designs and jumped into 3d.

![45015e0925f844138e57559e251e98e4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/45015e0925f844138e57559e251e98e4IMG_0321.JPG)

Same with Batman and Superman, it all starts with playing around and finding an angle, a time period, a feeling, or a silhouette. I do love to achieve a crafty look when doing things in 3d, that stop motion look, so using tools that enable that sort of hands-on feeling are things I like to explore in the process of making these.

![40bdf959052a449f90cce4fd7977474e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/40bdf959052a449f90cce4fd7977474eIMG_0343.jpg)![ea59ecd457fe4f20a4bb8d6f6fd10d00](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/ea59ecd457fe4f20a4bb8d6f6fd10d00IMG_0328.PNG)

# **How did you use Marvelous Designer in the artwork?**

So Marvelous Designer's way of letting you design the clothes like you would in real life gives a feeling that the outfit was made for real, there is something different about a patterned outfit from a regular modeled one because the patterns give you some restrictions like you have in real life, you are dealing with real scale, fitting, some things are impossible and creating with a tool like Marvelous give me that sort of good restriction that can enable real and believable clothing.

So the thinking is if these characters were stop-motion dolls and you had to make their outfits, how you do that in 3d, the weird body shapes require a good understanding of cutting the patterns and trying outfits because is not like putting a sack of potato on them, I wanted the suits to be tailored to be flowing with their designs, and so having that realtime feedback that marvelous give you is amazing.

![15b1c5cd6f884f9fbdd35533e0b918ef](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/15b1c5cd6f884f9fbdd35533e0b918efScreenshot%202025-03-10%20134425.png)![0d4b0b2466c74aa3bfc2dab1a396c207](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/0d4b0b2466c74aa3bfc2dab1a396c207Screenshot%202025-03-10%20134635.png)

I start modeling the character's body in c4d or Zbrush, trying to get the silhouettes and proportions close to the drawings, and already thinking about how some contact points, like shoulders, hips, arms and will fill in or leave space for the fabric to settle, they can be simple shapes but when I bring them into marvelous I try to respect their body.

![0f0f98bf678f4030be82c3305b88c246](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/0f0f98bf678f4030be82c3305b88c246Screenshot%202025-03-10%20140202.png)![b91be76280da4cb7ba0383e039f4cdc7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/b91be76280da4cb7ba0383e039f4cdc7Screenshot%202025-03-10%20140415.png)![98d797b93d864aa7b4e16273a4ef0cd4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/98d797b93d864aa7b4e16273a4ef0cd4Screenshot%202025-03-10%20135354.png)

I start with big shapes and start to cut and pin and break down as I get the flow I want. Sometimes if the character has pants or a jacket, I try to find a real pattern and start from there as I adapt to their weird body proportions, I want their costumes to make sense and give that feeling it was handmade, so knowing how a jacket is made I essential to break it apart into something else, I am not a fashion designer but is quite similar process of designing.

![dd7f95e44b17487288d569f64493acee](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/dd7f95e44b17487288d569f64493aceeScreenshot%202025-03-10%20134329.png)![6eb1dd8bc4e54a968046fb9ebe017eb2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/6eb1dd8bc4e54a968046fb9ebe017eb2Screenshot%202025-03-10%20134559.png)![f162aa4cfc394de0b7ec9cd1a0bc87a5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/f162aa4cfc394de0b7ec9cd1a0bc87a5Screenshot%202025-03-10%20134743.png)![901467037b204fd6bd6e1cb575a4b9ed](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/901467037b204fd6bd6e1cb575a4b9edScreenshot%202025-03-10%20134047.png)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

I am not a technical 3d guy, I started using 3d tools around 2017 at the same time these tools were starting to become more real-time, and less technical, so, in the same way, I was attracted to render engines that would allow me to see in real-time and work as a photographer figuring out organically the lighting, the same happened with marvelous, I saw how it had a similar way of letting you make decisions in real-time and it got my interest. When it comes to animation pipelines, although Marvelous has an animation feature, the studios I worked at usually worked traditionally, because the animations sometimes need some specific controlling, but I always tried to learn and experiment with it since is such a great tool.

# **Can you give us a quick overview of the different tools used in your pipeline?**

My pipeline is around Cinema 4D and the tools around it like Redshift Render, and Zbrush for sculpting, I do use sometimes Substance Painter which is amazing for bringing stitches and all these little details., But usually, I start in C4D getting some blocking done, and testing ideas, and then I move into specific tools for modeling or look dev, for the need to get me more depth beyond what C4D can offer.

![41ed1436815448dda98bb214efcce3ea](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/41ed1436815448dda98bb214efcce3ea1939%20%280-00-19-06%29.png)![34bd90b720f8439c8bb0762df3cbdf03](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/34bd90b720f8439c8bb0762df3cbdf031939%20%280-00-06-10%29.png)![a10e63d405a8441ca1dba7234a5abdeb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/a10e63d405a8441ca1dba7234a5abdebSPIDERMAN%202%20%280-00-19-18%29.png)![cfdb77c2b8964ef8890cdf402c6ba6c3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/cfdb77c2b8964ef8890cdf402c6ba6c3SPIDERMAN%202%20%280-00-18-04%29.png)

# **Do you have any other projects that you have worked on using Marvelous Designer that you can share with us?**

Yes, there are some characters I have used. Sometimes it is faster to generate a piece of outfit with Marvelous than to try to model it, and the quality is so good that is a go-to tool.

# **How can you describe your overall experience of the use of the Marvelous Designer?**

I think it is great software, is simple and very intuitive to use, there are enough YouTube tutorials for some specific things that might be harder to achieve, but for me, it was always very reliable, and the real-time interactivity you get with your designs is a game changer to create and have fun with it.

[Website](https://www.untitledarmy.com)

[Behance](https://www.behance.net/untitledarmy)

[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/untitledarmy/)

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/305547289fb245d4856ac53e4fdda6cf544543218568787.67a3839b2b9bd.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/ad48fe697d3f4379aa4440537ec16c42544543218568787.67a3839b2b9bd.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/6492e2232a2e426b8c0863d2d7636647/images/b8030f9f50bc4cbdb3c425ad0a6f6b76544543218568787.67a3839b2b9bd.png)

title: Trim UVs are so messed up when exported
content:
Hi I'm currently working on a project making a jacket that has a fireman's clasp and an brand logo emblem on it. There are in total of 4 imported trims as obj from blender: The TC on the chest each and the fireman's clasp(male and female). Everything went fine until I've exported to blender, and found out that the uvs for the trim were somehow interconnected to each other like a web like in the 2nd image. I know if I export the trim separately from the garments would make no problem, but I need an animation for both garments and the trims altogether. Even if I uncheck the 'unified uv coordinates' when exporting, the uv just goes crazy in another way like the 4th image. the UVs from the exported trims are somehow exploded and some faces are partially missing. what should I do from preventing the trim uvs to go crazy? Below is the Google Drive Link for the zprj file since its too big

<https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m4Of2hzbgKvr7d9t3WUNB_ayzQOEz77v/view?usp=sharing>

![ba29f21ace0a4d509258c06207548b49](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/347d9733c8894601a825516253a440ea/images/ba29f21ace0a4d509258c06207548b49%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-04-03%20140059.png)

![72fd27fce629400e8e0bffec98a62dce](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202504/347d9733c8894601a825516253a440ea/images/72fd27fce629400e8e0bffec98a62dce%EC%8A%A4%ED%81%AC%EB%A6%B0%EC%83%B7%202025-04-03%20140237.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hello, thank you for reporting the issue. We are currently working with the tech support team to determine whether it is a bug. We will get back to you soon!
content_description: This webpage aims to seek guidance on resolving UV mapping issues in Blender for a jacket project featuring a fireman's clasp and custom trims, while maintaining the integrity of both garment and trim animations.
